steps.description:
A Buzzer is used for making sounds.


Follow these steps:
  1. On the left side of the screen, there's a menu. This is where you can find all the coding blocks.

  2. Look for Buzzer in the menu and find the coding block that produces sound Notes. Drag it to the coding area.

  3. Select your robot.
  4. Click on the Stop button (to stop any program in the robot) and then the Play button to run the code.

  5. Have fun experimenting with the block! Try picking different notes like A4, B4, etc., and play around with the duration (how many seconds the sound lasts).



Play an F4 note for 3 seconds.

Just like we measure how long something is in centimeters, we can also measure sound using Hertz (Hz).

High-pitched is sharp, like a whistle. Low-pitched is dull, like a drumbeat. The bigger the Hertz number, the higher the pitch of the sound.

Besides using different Notes (A4, B4, etc), we can also use the Buzzer Tone block to make sound.



Practise these steps:
  1. Find a Buzzer coding block that controls the Tone of the Buzzer and drag it to the coding area.
  2. Select your robot.
  3. Click on the Stop button (to stop any program in the robot) and then the Play button to run the code.
  4. Test out different tones with values from 200Hz to 8000Hz.



1. Drag out two Tone blocks and stack them together. In Blockly, the code will run from top to bottom.

2. Play a higher pitch tone for 2 seconds, followed by a lower pitch tone for 2 seconds.

An LCD is used for displaying text. 


Perform the following:
  1. Find the LCD coding block on the menu and drag it to the coding area.

  2. Type some text on the Display Text box.
  3. Click on the Stop button (to stop any program in the robot) and then the Play button to run the code.
  4. Explore the block with different text and duration.



Display your name on the LCD for 5 seconds.

Do you know you can control your display position?

Perform the following:
  1. Using the LCD coding block, display "X".
  2. Change the Row number to 1 and observe what happen when you run the code.
  3. Change the Column number to 5 and observe what happen when you run the code again



Display "LOL" at the bottom right corner of the LCD.

If you want to leave notes or describe things in your program, you can use Comment blocks. 

 

Practise this:
  1. Take a Comment block from the menu and bring it to the coding area.
  2. Type some words in it.
  3. Run the program. Does anything happen?
  4. Comment blocks are not code so they will not have any effect. 

Use a Comment block to answer this riddle:

         

You will need to use comment blocks to answer some questions later.

Blockly can only run one column of code. If you have multiple columns of codes, they will all be run but the order depends on when they are created.

  

You can disable blocks that you do not want to run using the disable button.
  1. Drag out a sound block.
  2. Click on the sound block to select it.
  3. Find the "disable" button (an icon with a cross in a circle) and click on it a few times. You should see the sound block change colour.

  4. Try running the code when it is in different colours.
